identificationModule.briefTitle: Apatinib Combined With cdk4/6i in First-line Treatment for HR+/HER2- SNF4 Subtype Breast Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: Study of Efficacy of Apatinib Combined With cdk4/6i in First-line Treatment for HR+/HER2- SNF4 Subtype Advanced Breast Cancer (Open, Randomized, Phase III)

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a randomized, controlled, open-label, phase III study to explore the efficacy and safety of Apatinib in combination with standard first-line endocrine therapy for the HR+/ HER2-SNF4 subtype of advanced breast cancer. The study was used to explore the efficacy of Apatinib in combination with standard endocrine therapy.

armGroups.label: Arm-A
armGroups.description: Apatinib combined with cdk4/6i and Endocrine therapy.

interventions.name: Apatinib
interventions.description: Apatinib is a kind of TKI inhibitor.

interventions.name: CDK4/6 Inhibitor
interventions.description: Dalpiciclib (SHR6390) is a kind of CDK4/6 inhibitor that has demonstrated tolerability and preliminary clinical activity in patients with heavily pretreated hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.

interventions.name: Aromatase inhibitor and Fulvestrant
interventions.description: Endocrine therapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibitors is the standard first-line therapy for advanced luminal breast cancer. Investigators choose endocrine therapy including Letrozole, Anastrozole, Exemestane, and Fulvestrant. Postmenopausal participants should use Goserelin.

primaryOutcomes.description: The interval from randomization until the first occurrence of disease progression (according to RECIST 1.1) or death from any cause, which ever occurs first.

secondaryOutcomes.description: CBR is the total percentage of participants who achieved a complete response, partial response, or had stable disease for 6 months or more.
ORR is defined as the proportion of participants who have a complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) based on BICR and investigator assessment using RECIST 1.1.
OS is defined as the time from randomisation until the date of death due to any cause.
Number of adverse events according to NCI-CTCAE Version 5.0 per each treatment arm.
